INDEPENDENT DATA-INTEGRITY ASSESSMENT (skip_task_activation? drop-vs-defer), verified against actual code, not the design doc's own argument:

Traced the full call chain independently: (1) resolve_parent_token_record_id/2 (engine.ex:2345-2357) proves every prepared_children entry's parent_token_record_id is drawn from persisted_token_ids = MapSet.new(original_active_tokens, ...) -- the completing task's OWN instance's live tokens -- so parent_token.instance_id in the cascade (sub_process.ex:959, via load_parent_context/2) is structurally guaranteed equal to parent_instance_id (engine.ex:2412), confirming the design's central equality claim rather than trusting it. (2) append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6 (engine.ex:2502-2521) is a plain, unconditional Enum.reduce over the SAME prepared_children list the skip predicate (Enum.any?, engine.ex:2428-2431) inspects -- every entry that makes the predicate true unconditionally reaches SubProcess.append_start_multi/7 -> maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6's :completed clause (sub_process.ex:481-508) for that same entry; the boolean and the actual cascade trigger read the identical child_initial_state.status field off the identical struct, so they cannot drift apart. (3) When the cascade succeeds, build_completion_write_steps/12 (sub_process.ex:944-972) appends {:task_records, parent_instance_id} using a freshly re-read seed_state.pending_task_nodes (load_parent_context/2, sub_process.ex:1070-1111, real DB reads executed inside the still-open transaction) -- since call (1) is never composed into the Multi in this case, this fresh read cannot see any row call (1) would have inserted (there is no ordering race: the step simply does not exist). Task activation genuinely happens from the more-advanced snapshot; it is deferred, not dropped, confirmed structurally, not by inspection alone. (4) sub_process.ex (the cascade's own module) has ZERO diff in this change (confirmed via git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex, empty) -- the error-handling branch of maybe_chain_synchronous_completion (append_completion_multi/5 failing -> ExecutionError.append_multi/3, flipping parent_instance_id's own projection to :error) is pre-existing, unmodified behavior, not new to this fix; and pre-fix, this same failure scenario would have aborted the WHOLE transaction (including call (1)'s writes) via the collision RuntimeError anyway, so no tenant-visible regression is introduced by the skip. In all reachable single-collision cases, a tenant never observes a silently-missing task row under a projection claiming :completed/:active -- either the more-complete call (2) writes land, or the instance is explicitly flipped to :error.

FINDING (MINOR, not a gate failure on THIS diff -- filed for follow-up, does not block this fix): the fix's skip_task_activation? predicate (Enum.any?, first-level only) correctly prevents the call(1)-vs-call(2) collision ISS-0392 reports, but does NOT address a structurally distinct, second collision class this review discovered while tracing append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6: if a single hop chain's prepared_children contains TWO OR MORE entries that each independently complete synchronously (e.g., a prior PARALLEL_GATEWAY split landing two persisted, active tokens that both reach their own SUB_PROCESS node in the same hop chain -- resolve_parent_token_record_id/2's own split/join guard only rejects a DERIVED/unpersisted token_id reaching such a node, not two already-persisted tokens each independently doing so), each entry's own cascade call (sub_process.ex:966-972) would independently attempt {:task_records, parent_instance_id} for the SAME parent_instance_id, since all such children share one parent -- an unaddressed call(2)-vs-call(2) collision, structurally identical to ISS-0392's own bug but for a different trigger. This is transaction-scoped (rolls back cleanly on Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3's RuntimeError, same crash/rollback shape as the pre-fix bug, not a silent tenant-data-drop) so it does not fail INV-8 as scoped to THIS diff -- it is a pre-existing gap in the underlying engine, not introduced or worsened by this change, and the design doc itself never claims to close it (its own §3 scope is limited to the grandparent-cascade case, OQ-2). Recommend ORCH file this as a new issue via ISSUE_QUEUE.md (distinct from ISS-0392) for ISSUE-FIXER to assess reachability against REQ-062's graph-validation rules, same treatment as the design doc's own OQ-2.

issues.description: Second, structurally distinct Ecto.Multi :task_records collision class discovered during this review: two or more prepared_children entries in the SAME hop chain each completing synchronously (e.g. via a prior PARALLEL_GATEWAY split landing multiple already-persisted active tokens that each independently reach their own SUB_PROCESS node) would each independently append {:task_records, parent_instance_id} from build_completion_write_steps/12 (sub_process.ex:966-972) for the SAME parent_instance_id, colliding identically to ISS-0392's own bug. Not addressed by this fix (which only prevents the call(1)-vs-call(2) collision) and not introduced by this diff -- pre-existing in unmodified sub_process.ex. Transaction-scoped rollback on collision, not a silent data-integrity violation, so not a BLOCKER on this diff's own INV-8 scope. Recommend filing as a new issue for ISSUE-FIXER to assess reachability, distinct from ISS-0392.
